chunks: And the seeking of forgiveness of Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became evident to him that he was an enemy of God, he broke away from him. Indeed, Abraham was forbearing and forgiving.
ai.seo_question: Why did Abraham stop praying for his father?
ai.summary: Shia exegetes emphasize that this verse establishes the principle of *al-Bara' min al-Kuffar* (disassociation from disbelievers), showing that Abraham's initial supplication was a temporary concession based on his promise, which was revoked upon the confirmation of his father's enmity with God. This narrative underscores that familial piety (*Birr al-Walidayn*) is subordinate to monotheism (*Tawhid*), a key tenet in Shia jurisprudence, while simultaneously affirming Abraham's attributes of *Awah* (frequent supplicant) and *Halim* (forbearing).
